items.q: At the checkout, the ______ scanned my items and asked if I wanted a bag.
items.vi: Ở quầy tính tiền, nhân viên thu ngân quét các món hàng của tôi và hỏi tôi có cần túi không.
items.explanation: The clue is at the checkout ... scanned my items — the job of taking payment in a shop, so cashier. ✗ customer — the person buying, not scanning; ✗ accountant — keeps a company's financial records; ✗ banker — works in a bank, not at a shop till.

items.q: Thousands of ______ cheered when the striker scored in the last minute.
items.vi: Hàng nghìn khán giả reo hò khi tiền đạo ghi bàn ở phút cuối.
items.explanation: People watching a sports event are spectators; the clue is cheered when the striker scored. ✗ witnesses — people who see a crime or accident; ✗ observers — people who watch officially to check or report; ✗ audiences — 'audience' is a group noun for one crowd at a show, so 'thousands of audiences' would mean thousands of separate crowds.

items.q: My sister's ______ in the chess final was a boy who had never lost a game.
items.vi: Đối thủ của chị tôi trong trận chung kết cờ vua là một cậu bé chưa từng thua ván nào.
items.explanation: The person you play against is your opponent; the clue is in the chess final ... a boy who had never lost. ✗ partner — someone on your side in a pair; ✗ colleague — someone you work with; ✗ teammate — a member of your own team, not the person you face.

items.q: The ______ blew her whistle and told the children to get out of the pool.
items.vi: Nhân viên cứu hộ thổi còi và bảo bọn trẻ ra khỏi hồ bơi.
items.explanation: The clue is blew her whistle ... out of the pool: a lifeguard watches swimmers and keeps them safe. ✗ bodyguard — protects one person from attack; ✗ doorman — stands at a building's entrance; ✗ guardian — the adult legally responsible for a child.

items.q: A famous ______ with two million subscribers reviews new phones on her video channel every week.
items.vi: Một vlogger nổi tiếng với hai triệu người đăng ký đánh giá điện thoại mới trên kênh video của cô ấy mỗi tuần.
items.explanation: The clues are video channel and subscribers: a vlogger (video + blogger) makes videos. ✗ blogger — writes text posts on a website; ✗ editor — checks and corrects other people's writing; ✗ reporter — collects and writes news for a newspaper or TV.

items.q: Before buying the phone, Nam ______ a lot of research online.
items.vi: Trước khi mua điện thoại, Nam đã tìm hiểu rất nhiều trên mạng.
items.explanation: Research collocates with do: do research (like do homework, do an experiment). ✗ made — 'make' goes with creating something (make a decision, make a mistake), never research; ✗ took — 'take' goes with time, a test or a photo, not research; ✗ gave — 'give' goes with a talk or a presentation, not research.

items.q: Choose a ______ password so that nobody can get into your account.
items.vi: Hãy chọn một mật khẩu mạnh để không ai vào được tài khoản của bạn.
items.explanation: A password that is hard to guess is a strong password; the clue is so that nobody can get into your account. ✗ heavy — describes weight, rain or traffic, not passwords; ✗ hard — means difficult, but 'hard password' is not the collocation; ✗ powerful — describes engines, leaders or arguments, not passwords.

items.q: Please ______ attention when the referee explains the rules of the game.
items.vi: Hãy chú ý khi trọng tài giải thích luật của trận đấu.
items.explanation: The fixed collocation is pay attention = listen or watch carefully; the clue is when the referee explains the rules. ✗ give — you give someone a present or a hand; 'give attention' is not the idiom for listening carefully; ✗ take — 'take' does not pair with 'attention' at all; ✗ make — 'make' goes with an effort or a decision, not attention.

items.q: Even though it started to rain, the players ______ with the match until the referee stopped it.
items.vi: Dù trời bắt đầu mưa, các cầu thủ vẫn tiếp tục trận đấu cho đến khi trọng tài dừng lại.
items.explanation: A finished past story told in order — it started to rain, they carried on, the referee stopped it — uses the past simple: carried on. ✗ have carried on — present perfect cannot sit in a story told with past-simple 'started' and 'stopped'; ✗ carry on — present simple for a past event; ✗ had carried on — past perfect is for an action BEFORE another past action, but carrying on came after the rain started.

items.q: Lan: Where's Nam? / Nam's mum: He ______ football in the park at the moment.
items.vi: Lan: Nam đâu ạ? / Mẹ Nam: Nó đang đá bóng trong công viên.
items.explanation: At the moment means right now, so the present continuous is playing is needed. ✗ plays — present simple is for habits and facts, not an action in progress; ✗ has played — present perfect links past to present but does not describe what is happening now; ✗ played — past simple is for a finished action, but the game is still going on.

items.q: I ______ this phone for three years, so it's time to buy a new one.
items.vi: Tôi đã dùng chiếc điện thoại này ba năm rồi, nên đã đến lúc mua cái mới.
items.explanation: A situation that began in the past and continues to now, with for three years, takes the present perfect: have had. ✗ had — past simple would mean I no longer have it, but I still do (it's time to buy a new one); ✗ am having — 'have' meaning own is a state verb, not used in the continuous; ✗ have — present simple cannot carry 'for three years' back into the past.

items.q: By the time the shop opened, dozens of people ______ outside for hours.
items.vi: Đến lúc cửa hàng mở cửa, hàng chục người đã đứng chờ bên ngoài suốt mấy tiếng.
items.explanation: An activity that continued up to a past moment (by the time the shop opened) with a duration (for hours) takes the past perfect continuous: had been waiting. ✗ waited — past simple does not show the waiting happened before the opening; ✗ have waited — present perfect cannot combine with the past event 'opened'; ✗ were waiting — past continuous shows an action at that moment but does not carry 'for hours' up to it.

items.q: Lan: Do you know a shop called Phone World? / Nam: The name ______, but I can't remember where it is.
options: hits the nail on the head
items.vi: Lan: Cậu biết cửa hàng tên Phone World không? / Nam: Cái tên nghe quen quen, nhưng tớ không nhớ nó ở đâu.
items.explanation: Ring a bell = sound familiar; the clue is but I can't remember where it is. ✗ breaks the ice — makes people relax when they first meet; ✗ hits the nail on the head — says exactly the right thing; ✗ gets on my nerves — annoys me.

items.q: Our team played well in the first half but ______ after the break and lost 3-1.
items.vi: Đội chúng tôi chơi tốt ở hiệp một nhưng đuối sức sau giờ nghỉ và thua 3-1.
items.explanation: Run out of steam = lose energy and stop trying hard; the clue is played well in the first half but ... lost. ✗ hit the roof — got very angry; ✗ missed the boat — lost a chance by being too late; ✗ made ends meet — had just enough money to live on.

items.q: The shop ______ my request for a refund because I had lost the receipt.
items.vi: Cửa hàng đã từ chối yêu cầu hoàn tiền của tôi vì tôi làm mất hóa đơn.
items.explanation: Turn down = refuse a request or offer; the clue is because I had lost the receipt, a reason for refusing. ✗ turned up — arrived, or increased the volume; ✗ turned over — flipped something to the other side; ✗ turned off — switched off a machine or light.

items.q: Please don't ______ the money I owe you in front of my parents.
items.vi: Làm ơn đừng nhắc đến số tiền tớ nợ cậu trước mặt bố mẹ tớ.
items.explanation: Bring up = mention a subject; the clue is in front of my parents — the speaker doesn't want the debt mentioned. ✗ bring back — return something, or make you remember; ✗ bring about — cause a change to happen; ✗ bring in — introduce a rule, or earn money.

items.q: Nam paid full price in the shop. He ______ have bought the phone online, where the same model is much cheaper.
items.vi: Nam đã trả nguyên giá ở cửa hàng. Lẽ ra cậu ấy nên mua điện thoại trên mạng, nơi cùng mẫu đó rẻ hơn nhiều.
items.explanation: Should have + past participle criticises a past choice: it was a good idea but he didn't do it. The clue is paid full price although online is much cheaper. ✗ must have — a confident guess that something DID happen, but he did not buy online; ✗ can't have — a confident guess that something did NOT happen, not advice; ✗ needn't have — he did it but it wasn't necessary, yet he never bought online at all.

items.q: Lan ______ have spent much money at the market - she only bought a keyring.
items.vi: Lan không thể nào tiêu nhiều tiền ở chợ được - cô ấy chỉ mua một cái móc khóa.
items.explanation: Can't have + past participle = the speaker is sure something did NOT happen; the clue is she only bought a keyring. ✗ must have — sure it DID happen, the opposite of the evidence; ✗ should have — criticism that she ought to have spent much money, which makes no sense; ✗ needn't have — she spent a lot but didn't need to, yet she spent almost nothing.

items.q: The girl ______ phone was stolen on the bus reported it to the police.
items.vi: Cô gái có điện thoại bị lấy cắp trên xe buýt đã báo cảnh sát.
items.explanation: Whose shows possession — the girl's phone — and is followed directly by the noun phone. ✗ who — a subject pronoun for a person; it cannot stand before a noun ('who phone'); ✗ which — refers to a thing and also cannot stand before a noun here; ✗ whom — an object pronoun (the girl whom I saw), not a possessive.

items.q: The shop ______ I bought my headphones has closed down.
items.vi: Cửa hàng nơi tôi mua tai nghe đã đóng cửa rồi.
items.explanation: Where replaces 'in the shop' — a place — and is followed by a complete clause, I bought my headphones. ✗ which — needs a preposition for a place ('the shop from which I bought them'); ✗ that — also needs a preposition ('the shop that I bought them from'); ✗ whose — shows possession, but the shop owns nothing here.

items.q: There isn't ______ time left before the sale ends, so hurry up.
items.vi: Không còn nhiều thời gian trước khi đợt giảm giá kết thúc, nên nhanh lên.
items.explanation: Time (hours and minutes) is uncountable, and the sentence is negative (isn't), so it takes much. ✗ many — only with plural countable nouns (many days); ✗ a few — plural countable only, and 'a few' is not used after 'isn't'; ✗ few — plural countable only (few days).

items.q: Don't forget ______ your phone before the match; you'll want to take photos.
items.vi: Đừng quên sạc điện thoại trước trận đấu; cậu sẽ muốn chụp ảnh đấy.
items.explanation: Forget + to-infinitive = forget to do a task that is still to be done; the clue is before the match, a future job. ✗ charging — 'forget doing' means having no memory of something already done; ✗ charge — 'forget' is never followed by a bare infinitive; ✗ to charging — 'to' + -ing does not follow 'forget'.

items.q: The tickets were quite expensive; ______, the stadium was completely full.
items.vi: Vé khá đắt; tuy nhiên, sân vận động vẫn chật kín.
items.explanation: Two contrasting ideas (expensive but completely full) joined by a semicolon and a comma need the linking adverb however. ✗ therefore — an adverb, but it shows a result, and a full stadium is not the result of expensive tickets; ✗ because — a conjunction giving a reason; it cannot sit between ';' and ','; ✗ although — shows contrast but is a conjunction that must start a clause ('although the tickets were expensive'), not stand alone between ';' and ','.

items.q: If I ______ so much on clothes last month, I could buy those trainers now.
items.vi: Nếu tháng trước tôi không tiêu quá nhiều vào quần áo thì bây giờ tôi đã có thể mua đôi giày thể thao đó.
items.explanation: A mixed conditional: an unreal past condition (last month) takes the past perfect hadn't spent, and its present result uses could + verb (could buy ... now). ✗ didn't spend — past simple after 'if' makes a second conditional about the present, but 'last month' is finished; ✗ haven't spent — present perfect cannot be used with 'last month' and does not form an unreal condition; ✗ wouldn't spend — 'would' belongs in the result clause, not after 'if'.

items.q: Only after the final whistle ______ how tired he was.
items.vi: Chỉ sau tiếng còi kết thúc Nam mới nhận ra mình mệt đến thế nào.
items.explanation: When a sentence starts with the limiting phrase Only after ..., the auxiliary and subject are inverted like a question: did Nam realise. ✗ Nam realised — normal word order, but 'Only after' at the front forces inversion; ✗ Nam did realise — 'did' after the subject is emphasis, not inversion; ✗ realised Nam — inverts the main verb instead of the auxiliary 'did'.
